predecessors.name: Ottoman Tripolitania
predecessors.text: 'In the mountains near Sidi Rafaa' (Bayda) he built the Zawiya Bayda "White Monastery"', the order's first seat in Libya

successors.name: Italian Libya
successors.text: what was left of the Senussi land when 'Badoglio proclaimed the end of the campaign' in January 1932: Cyrenaica beyond the coastal lowlands, Jaghbub and Kufra, which had fallen in 1926 and 1931

rulers.name: Muhammad ibn Ali as-Senussi (the Grand Senussi)
Idris (later King Idris of Libya)
rulers.title: Head of the order; Emir of Cyrenaica from October 1920

ledger.x: 1843: Muhammad ibn Ali as-Senussi returns to Libya and builds the Zawiya Bayda in the Jebel Akhdar.
1855: the order moves its seat to Jaghbub.
1894: the Senussi take up the Kufra oases.
October 1912: the Senussi hold the Cyrenaican interior as the Ottomans leave.
October 1912: the interior stays out of Italian hands.
26 January 1923: the Second Italo-Senussi War begins.
January 1932: the last Cyrenaican resistance ends.
January 1932: Cyrenaica passes under Italian control.
January 1932: the same hand-over recorded against the umbrella, as italian-africa ledger 40 does.
January 1932: the Senussi state ends in Cyrenaica.

wars.name: Italo-Senussi hostilities after the Treaty of Ouchy
wars.outcome: The Italians were confined to coastal enclaves: 'besieged in seven enclaves' at the end of 1912 and, 'by 1 August 1915', concentrated in Tripoli, Homs, Benghazi, Derna, Cyrene and Tobruk.

wars.name: Senussi Campaign
wars.outcome: The order fought 'in Egypt from November 1915 until February 1917' and 'in the Sudan from March to December 1916'; 'the British sent an expeditionary force against them known as the Senussi Campaign'.

wars.name: Second Italo-Senussi War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: the northern lowlands regained in 1923-1924, Jaghbub occupied early 1926, Kufra seized 1931, Mukhtar captured September 1931 and executed, Badoglio proclaims the end of the campaign in January 1932.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for the order's land: the early shapes are discs round its seats, the later ones the gazetteer's Cyrenaica less the places the pages say fell.
